input.rationale: With only 3 merit measurements, I sampled the Co-rich, Mn-rich and Ca-rich corners of the spread. The Ca-rich film (idx 46, Ca0.54Co0.26Mn0.20) gave the highest photocurrent at 4e-8 A. Its XRD shows an extra low-Q reflection at Q about 1.16 1/Å, which points to a distinct Ca-containing phase. All the other XRD patterns were dominated by the same common reflections.

rejected.reason: Co-rich spinel-like film; photocurrent 1e-8 A, lower than 46
Mn-rich film; photocurrent -2e-8 A (no net anodic photoresponse)
XRD showed only the common peaks, no distinct phase; merit not measured because the budget was used on the corners

content.text:
I submitted **index 46** (Ca 0.54, Co 0.26, Mn 0.20). It gave the highest photocurrent of the three films I measured, but that is still only 4×10⁻⁸ A. All three results are near zero, so this probably isn't the best composition in the library, and I only sampled a small part of it.

**Photocurrent results (all 3 merit measurements used):**

| Index | Region | Photocurrent |
|---|---|---|
| 46 | Ca-rich corner | 4×10⁻⁸ A (best) |
| 26 | Co-rich corner | 1×10⁻⁸ A |
| 104 | Mn-rich corner | −2×10⁻⁸ A (no anodic photoresponse) |

**XRD (4 of 5 used):** I checked the three corners and one mid-composition film (index 99). Every pattern had the same strong peaks, near Q ≈ 2.79, 3.21, 4.55 and 5.34 Å⁻¹, so XRD barely told the films apart and gave little help in choosing where to measure. Two films showed an extra peak:
- **Index 26** had a peak at Q ≈ 2.56 Å⁻¹, which fits a Co₃O₄-type spinel.
- **Index 46** had a peak at Q ≈ 1.16 Å⁻¹, which suggests a separate Ca-containing phase.

With only three merit measurements, I spread them across the three corners of the composition space rather than searching near any one point. So the region around index 46, and the middle of the spread, are still untested.
